acceptance: `test.yml`'s `medium` job syncs the locked `_project/scripts` runtime before running tests, as the other four jobs do.

A fast test fails when a provisioning step present in one of the five medium-suite jobs is missing from another; an explicit allowlist covers only differences a job needs (coverage tooling, matrix-specific steps).
The test is shown to work by removing the `_project/scripts` sync from any one job and seeing it fail.

description:
The medium suite (`-m "medium and not (slow or stress or resource_heavy or live_integration)"` or the nightly core integration suite) runs in five jobs that each define their own setup: `medium-test` in `ci.yml`; `medium-test` in `trunk.yml` and in `trunk-coverage.yml`, which `ci.yml` calls as `trunk-lane-plain` and `trunk-lane-coverage`; the `integration` core suite in `nightly-v2.yml`; and `medium` in `test.yml`, which runs on pushes and PRs to `release`. Nothing checks that they provision the same things.

Live defect: since #3725, `test_installed_runtime_handshake_exposes_registered_batch_tools` runs `uv run --offline` against `_project/scripts` and needs the locked `uv sync --project _project/scripts --locked` step. `ci.yml`, `trunk.yml`, `trunk-coverage.yml` and `nightly-v2.yml` have it; `test.yml`'s `medium` job runs only `uv sync --group dev`, so the next release PR or push will fail that test.

How the drift showed: on #3725 the sync was first added to `ci.yml` and `nightly-v2.yml` only. `tests/unit/workflows` passed (1,033 tests); the gap showed only when the full CI run failed both trunk-lane `medium-test (shard 0)` jobs. The trunk lanes run on PRs, so they caught it before merge; drift in `nightly-v2.yml` or `test.yml` shows only in a nightly or release run.
